metadata.title: Faria et al. (2006) — fully restrained through-thickness strip (Fig. 9; bound for Figs. 17–18)
metadata.validation_method: Digitized paper curves. Thermal: Fig. 7a/7b (measured + paper 1D model + air) and Fig. 8b (hydration degree). Mechanical: Fig. 9a (with creep), Fig. 9b (no creep, all three depths), Fig. 17 (2D/3D P3), Fig. 18 (eps_x bottom). Calibration: Fig. 5 pseudo-adiabatic.
metadata.validation_target: Peak T 33.5 C at ~0.62 d at the centre (Fig. 8a) and ~31.5 C at 5 cm from the top (Fig. 7a); alpha 0.689 at 1 d and 0.925 at 9 d (Fig. 8b); sigma_x at the centre dipping to ~-0.75 MPa at ~0.7 d and reaching ~+2.9 MPa at 9 d (Fig. 9a).
metadata.notes:
STATUS 2026-08-23: this file had NEVER run to completion. Three hard blockers were fixed: (1) the mesh in input/ was stale -- built for different group names (surface_top / restraint_left vs the file's face_top / face_left) and a different width (0.05 vs 0.10 m); (2) materials.concrete.displacement had no 'rho', a hard KeyError; (3) the paper's nu=0.2 with DPL n=0.3 cannot be expressed on oofem at all (see below).

PORTED FROM THE SIBLING ../thermal/benchmark.json, which had already solved what this file listed as unsolved: the calibrated affinity parameters (B1/B2/alpha_inf/eta/Hu/T_ref -- this file previously carried unfitted placeholders and said so), the real air-temperature history on the top face (input/ambient_temperature_fig7a.csv was already on disk while this file pinned u_ref to a constant 17 C and called the history 'missing'), and the 17.25 C placement temperature. Result: peak T at the centre is now 33.5 C at 0.62 d, matching Fig. 8a exactly; before the port it was 36.5 C at 0.54 d.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE 1 -- Poisson's ratio is FORCED to 0.3. oofem reads one input key "n" as BOTH Poisson's ratio and the DPL exponent (verified: rheoChM.h:52 and doublepowerlaw.h:46 both define it as "n"; DoublePowerLawMaterial::initializeFrom reads it twice). Table 2 needs nu=0.2 and n=0.3. The creep law was kept intact and nu sacrificed, because the nu error is a first-order scale factor that can be undone (sigma ~ 1/(1-nu), so x0.875 -- see the sx_*_nu_corr queries) whereas changing n would corrupt the creep kinetics irreversibly.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE 2 -- ageing stiffness is IGNORED. Table 2 gives Ec = 29e9*alpha^0.5, but oofem's doublepowerlaw has no alpha-dependent E0, so stiffness sits at 29 GPa from t=0. This is the dominant remaining error and it is visible in fig9_creep_vs_nocreep.png: the run's compressive peak is -2.26 MPa (-1.98 nu-corrected) against Fig. 9a's ~-0.75 MPa, i.e. it falls between the paper's with-creep and no-creep curves rather than on the with-creep one. At the compressive peak alpha ~ 0.45, so the paper's E is 29*sqrt(0.45) = 19.5 GPa, two thirds of what this run uses. The final tension (+2.98 MPa raw, Fig. 9a ~+2.9) agrees well, but partly by cancellation of the two divergences above -- do not read it as validation.

Hydration reaches alpha = 0.860 at 9 d against Fig. 8b's 0.925; the affinity fit was made against temperature (Fig. 7), not against alpha, so this is the fit's residual, not a bug.

This mesh is the Sec. 4.2 'infinite slab' (eps_x = eps_z = 0), which is Fig. 9. Fig. 17 P3 is ~86% of that stress and Fig. 18 is a 3D sensor with finite pile restraint -- expect the same shape there, not the same amplitude.

power_law_creep._comment: Canonical key. No source_field — DPL reads its own history. Do not rename (thermal_strain vs thermal_aging ambiguity).

temperature._comment_rho_cp: INFERRED: Table 1 qc=2400 J/m3K is a unit error → 2400 kJ/m3K = rho*cp

degree_of_hydration._comment_source: CALIBRATED: taken verbatim from the sibling thermal benchmark (../thermal/benchmark.json), which fitted these against Fig. 7a/7b. Previously this file carried unfitted placeholders (B1=3.6e-4, B2=5.0e-4, alpha_inf=0.85, eta=6.0, Hu=450, T_ref=293.15) and its own notes flagged them MISSING/CALIBRATE -- with those the peak temperature, and therefore every stress in Fig. 9, was meaningless.
degree_of_hydration._comment_T_ref: PAPER-ADJACENT: 25 C = 298.15 K. KELVIN only (the BC/IC fields stay degC).
degree_of_hydration._comment_sanity: dT_ad = Hu*c*alpha_inf/(rho*cp) = 420.2e3*285*0.93/(2400*1000) = 46.4 K. Fig. 5's pseudo-adiabatic curve rises 15 -> 61.4 C = 46.4 K. Exact match -- this is what fig5_pseudo_adiabatic.csv is for.

displacement._comment_E_nu: PAPER_VALUE: Table 2 Ec = 29e9*alpha^0.5 Pa. On oofem the ageing keys (alpha_0/alpha_inf/a_E/E_min) are SILENTLY IGNORED -- stiffness stays 29 GPa from t=0, which overstates early compression. RISKY, unchanged from before.
displacement._comment_plane: Default plane strain + ux=0 on both sides = εx=εz=0 = infinite slab (Fig. 9). Do NOT set plane_stress.
displacement._comment_rho: Same 2400 kg/m3 as the temperature section. Required by the builder (oofem materials always take a density); inert in a quasi-static analysis. Its absence was a hard KeyError -- this file had never been run to completion.
displacement._comment_nu_FORCED:
FORCED TO 0.3, NOT the paper's 0.2. VERIFIED oofem limitation: rheoChM.h:52 defines _IFT_RheoChainMaterial_n as "n" and doublepowerlaw.h:46 defines _IFT_DoublePowerLawMaterial_n as "n" -- the SAME input key. DoublePowerLawMaterial::initializeFrom calls MaxwellChainMaterial::initializeFrom first (which reads "n" into Poisson's ratio, rheoChM.C:585) and then reads "n" again into the power-law exponent (doublepowerlaw.C:47). Poisson's ratio and the DPL exponent therefore CANNOT differ on this backend, and Table 2 needs nu=0.2 with n=0.3.
CHOICE: keep the paper's creep law intact (phi1/m/n all from Table 2) and accept the wrong Poisson's ratio, because the nu error is a clean first-order SCALE factor that can be undone: under full in-plane restraint sigma_x = -E*alphaT*dT/(1-nu), so this run is 1/(1-0.3) / (1/(1-0.2)) = 1.143x too stiff and sigma_x_paper ~ 0.875 * sigma_x_sim. See the sx_*_nu_corr queries. The alternative (nu=n=0.2) would instead corrupt the creep kinetics -- (t-t')^0.2 vs ^0.3 is ~19% less creep compliance at 8 d -- which is NOT correctable by a scale factor and would undermine the one phenomenon Sec. 4.2 is about.

thermal_strain._comment: PAPER_VALUE: Table 2 alphaT = 10e-6 /K. T_strain_free_ref MUST equal the placement temperature (concrete is stress-free at casting), so it moves with the initial condition to 17.25 C. Leaving it at 20 while the IC was 17.25 would impose a spurious -2.75 K thermal strain at t=0. DEGREES CELSIUS.

power_law_creep._comment: PAPER_VALUE: Table 2 DPL phi1=2.26, m=0.35, n=0.3. E0 taken as Ec1=29 GPa. Extra keys (fi1, m, alpha) are what oofem doublepowerlaw actually reads — keep both spellings until the builder is documented. age_at_start_days ASSUMED 0.01 d so t0^{-m} is finite. Time unit of DPL in oofem is DAYS.

initial_conditions._comment: Placement temperature, ported from the sibling thermal benchmark, which calibrated it against Fig. 7a/7b (first measured point 17.5 C). The previous 20.0 was inferred from Fig. 18 -- a DIFFERENT sensor and a different (3D) analysis -- and ran the whole slab ~3 K too hot: peak T_centre 36.5 C against Fig. 8a's 33.5 C. DEGREES CELSIUS.

boundary_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: Table 1 h=4.5 W/m2K, soil 17 C

PAPER_VALUE h=7.5 W/m2K (Table 1). The air history is the digitized Fig. 7a environmental series, already present in input/ and already used by the sibling thermal benchmark -- this file previously pinned u_ref to a constant 17 C and noted the history as 'missing', which flattened the daily swing after day 5 that Sec. 4.2 says the boundary conditions were tuned to reproduce.
PAPER_VALUE 3D: bottom plane uz=0 (Sec. 4.4). Vertical faces remain thermally Robin-only.

reference_curves.label: Fig. 8b hydration degree (paper 1D)
reference_curves._comment: DIGITIZED 2026-08-23 from Fig. 8b by upper-envelope extraction at 300 dpi (x=0 at col 181.7, 88.12 px/day from the 1..9 digit centres; alpha=0 at row 753.5, 571.5 px/unit). The paper's Top/Centre/Bottom curves are nearly coincident (Sec. 4.2), so one curve represents all three; this is the Centre (upper) envelope. 0.689 at 1 d, 0.925 at 9 d.

queries.label: sigma_x top [Pa]
queries._comment: OOFEM field query, prefixed component. NOT type=stress (COMSOL-only).

queries.label: eps_x bot [-]
queries._comment: Total strain. Fig. 18 zeros the gauge at onset of cooling (~1 d).

queries.label: Equivalent adiabatic T [degC]
queries._comment: Reconstructs the adiabatic temperature this run's hydration implies: T0 + alpha*dT_ad with dT_ad = Hu*c*alpha_inf/(rho*cp) = 46.4 K. Fig. 5 starts at 15 C, so compare SHAPE and total rise, not absolute level.

queries.label: sigma_x top [MPa], nu-corrected
queries._comment: First-order correction for the forced nu=0.3 (see materials.concrete.displacement._comment_nu_FORCED): (1-0.3)/(1-0.2) = 0.875. Exact for the elastic restrained part; approximate once creep redistributes.
